clusters.note: The classic three-way. They differ ONLY in how far the top-left stroke closes: 开口己、半口已、闭口巳 — 'open-mouth jǐ, half-mouth yǐ, closed-mouth sì'. 己 (self) leaves a clear gap; 已 (already) closes it halfway; 巳 (6th earthly branch, the snake) seals it shut. Same three strokes, three characters.

examples.gloss: zìjǐ — oneself (己 = self; the mouth stays OPEN)
yǐjīng — already (已 = already; the mouth is HALF closed)
sìshí — the hour of the snake, 9–11am (巳 = 6th branch; the mouth is SHUT)

clusters.note: Two strokes each, mirrored. In 人 (person) the two strokes MEET at the apex. In 入 (to enter) the short stroke starts partway down the long one, so the top is a CROSSING, not a clean peak — and the long stroke is the one on the right.

The same two characters reversed. 不可 = 'cannot / must not'. 可不 is NOT its negation: it is either the 可不可… A-not-A frame ('can or can't…?') or, colloquially, 可不(是) = emphatic agreement ('isn't it just').

examples.gloss: Isn't it just! / That's so true! — 可不(是) = emphatic agreement
(I) simply must go. — 非…不可 = 'cannot not' = must

clusters.note: Same body shape. 西 (west) and the cover radical 襾 share the 西-form — 襾 is 西 with an extra horizontal stroke across the very top, and its top-only variant 覀 sits atop 要/票/覆. So a 西-looking top in those characters is the COVER radical, not 西 'west'.

examples.gloss: dōngxi — thing (lit. east-west); here 西 = west
yào — to want / important; its top is the 覀/襾 cover radical, NOT 西

clusters.note: 同族 — 西 is classified under Kangxi radical 146 襾 ('cover'). Historically one radical family: 西 became the everyday character 'west', while 襾 (and its top-form 覀) is the radical 'cover' seen atop 要/票/覆. Same origin, now distinct senses — the mirror image of a confusable, which shares a look but not an origin.

Kangxi radical 80, two glyph-forms of one slot. 毋 (wú, 'do not') is the authoritative dictionary radical; 母 ('mother') is the form actually seen in the characters classed under it (每/毒/毓). Distinguished by the inner marks — 母 has two dots, 毋 a single bar — so also easily confused.

Same 母-frame, three different inner marks — tell them apart by what's inside the box: 母 (mother) keeps the two nursing dots; 毋 (wú, 'do not') strikes a single bar through them — 'don't'; 毌 (guàn, 'pass through') runs the bar clear across. A 己/已/巳-style triple.

examples.gloss: mǔqīn — mother; 母 keeps the two dots
wúyōng — no need; 毋 = 'do not', one bar through
guàn — 毌 depicts piercing-through; it survives atop 贯 (毌+贝) 'pierce / string of cash'

clusters.note: The 'field with a line' family. 田 (field) is the closed grid. 由 (from / cause) is 田 with the central vertical pushing UP through the top. Its cousins extend the same stroke elsewhere: 甲 (jiǎ, first) pushes it DOWN through the bottom, 申 (shēn, to extend) through BOTH ends. Read 由 by the top-exit.

examples.gloss: zìyóu — freedom (由 = from / cause; the stroke exits the TOP)
tiándì — farmland (田 = field; the grid stays CLOSED)

clusters.note: Homophones — both read tā, both built on the 也 phonetic. The radical carries the sense: 亻(person) → 他 'he', 女(woman) → 她 'she'. The set's third member 它 (roof 宀 → 'it', for things and animals) is the same tā again; pick the character by its referent, not by the sound.

examples.gloss: tāmen — they (men / mixed group; 他 = he, person radical)
tāmen — they (all female; 她 = she, woman radical)
